{ "url": "https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets", "title": "Telegram Widgets", "family": "bot-api", "sha": "dfc14652a3a0a6e5b8405935a78f654abd956e0eb40cafcc33eacf7f2610919c", "checked_at": "2026-11-10T20:52:46.472228+00:00", "changed_at": "2026-11-10T17:50:04.877545+00:00", "error": null, "freshness": { "stale": false, "age_seconds": 170, "max_age_seconds": 21600, "refresh_error": null }, "body": "# Telegram Widgets Bots can send **widgets**: small interactive blocks drawn right inside a message. A widget is one self-contained HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript, at most 32 KB of HTML and 4 KB after compression. Telegram apps run it on the user's device in a sandbox with **no network access at all**, draw it in the style of the chat, and keep it running while it is on screen: a poll whose bars move as people vote, a price ticker, a board game for two in a group, a promo code that copies on a tap. A widget is **fixed code plus changeable state**. The code, its HTML, is set when the widget is sent and never changes. What changes is the widget's state, and only the bot writes it: the **chat state**, tied to one message and seen only in that chat, and the **shared state**, seen wherever the widget is shown. The widget reads its state and redraws when it changes. It cannot change the state itself, but it can ask the bot with small requests, the way a callback button does. Widgets live in the private chat with the bot, in groups, in messages sent via the bot in inline mode, and in forwards to any chat. Currently, in the production environment, widgets work only in the private chat with the bot. The rest works on the [test server](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability). A widget can also be a **shared widget**: one widget on the server, like a poll, that any number of messages show, with one shared state for all of them. This page is a guide to designing and implementing widgets, followed by the reference of the widget's JavaScript object `TelegramWidget`. The Bot API methods and types for widgets are in the [Bot API reference](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api). --- ### Introducing widgets #### Code and state A widget is fixed code plus changeable state. * **The code** (the HTML with its CSS and JavaScript) is set when the widget is sent and never changes, in a message or in a shared widget. No method replaces it. For a new layout, send a new widget, and old messages keep the old one. As with any media, the caption can be edited. * **The state** is what changes, and only the bot writes it. There are two kinds: + **chat state** (`chat_data`): tied to one message, seen only in that chat (shared by all members in a group), never carried by a forward. A game in progress, whose turn it is. + **shared state** (`public_data`): seen wherever the widget is shown. A static widget keeps it in the message, and a forward gets a copy as of the moment of forwarding. A [shared widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#static-and-shared-widgets) (one object with an identifier, like a poll) has one shared state for all its messages and forwards. Poll results, a price. * **The widget** reads its state, learns about changes through the `chatDataChanged` and `publicDataChanged` events, and cannot change its state itself: it can only ask the bot, with a [request](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#requests-to-the-bot). Details: [The widget's state](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#the-widgets-state). #### What a widget is * **One HTML document.** Inline `

It must not contain the NUL character (U+0000), or the server refuses it with `INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_HTML_INVALID`. The server compresses the HTML and refuses anything over the limits (`INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_TOO_LARGE`). Use [sendSharedWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendsharedwidget) to send an existing [shared widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#static-and-shared-widgets) again by its identifier, the way a photo is sent again by its `file_id`. ``` POST https://api.telegram.org/bot/sendWidget { "chat_id": 111111111, "html": "

Order #1042

2 × Margherita, 1 × Lemonade

…", "caption": "Order #1042: $23.50" } ``` On success the sent [Message](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#message) is returned, with its [widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widget): the HTML, the size anchors, the current state and, for a shared widget, its `id`. With `sendWidget`, the bot makes two choices, kept with the widget and carried by its forwards: | Parameter | What it does | | --- | --- | | `allow_queries` | The widget may send [requests](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#requests-to-the-bot) to the bot. Without it, every request to this widget is refused, everywhere. Allow requests only if the widget needs to talk to the bot: a ticker or a widget that only shows its state needs none. | | `is_shared` | Creates a shared widget: one object for the original, all its forwards and every message later sent with `sendSharedWidget`. Its forwards follow its shared state, and with `allow_queries` they may send requests too, on a tap (forwards: [test server only](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability)). A ticker without requests is `is_shared` without `allow_queries`. | Without `is_shared` the widget is **static**: everything stays in the message. Also pass the widget's initial [state](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#the-widgets-state), `public_data` and `chat_data`, and the size anchors `width` and `height` ([Sizes](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#sizes)) when you know them. The usual message parameters work as for a photo: a caption with its entities (and `show_caption_above_media`, which leaves [the time on the widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#the-time-in-the-corner)), an inline keyboard under the widget, a reply, a forum topic, `protect_content`. The caption can be changed later with [editMessageCaption](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagecaption), as for any media. The widget itself cannot be replaced: no method changes the HTML of a sent widget. #### The widget's state A widget is fixed code plus changeable state. The code never changes after sending, and the state is what the bot changes. Only the bot writes the state: when it sends the widget, and later with the [methods that change it](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#changing-the-state), never inside an answer to a request. The widget reads its state as `TelegramWidget.chatData` and `TelegramWidget.publicData` and cannot change it itself. It can only ask the bot. | Property | Chat state (`chat_data`) | Shared state (`public_data`) | | --- | --- | --- | | Tied to | one original message: in the bot's private chat with the user, in a group (shared by all its members), or sent via the bot | a static widget's message, or a shared widget (every message and forward that shows it) | | Seen | only in that chat | wherever the widget is shown | | In a forward | never | a copy as of the moment of forwarding for a static widget, the one current shared state for a shared widget | | Examples | a game in progress, whose turn it is, a code this user redeemed | poll results, a price, a score | | Changed by | [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata) on the original | [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata) on an original, or [editSharedWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editsharedwidgetdata) by the shared widget's identifier | | Reaches open widgets | at once, pushed by the server | pushed with the message for a static widget. For a shared widget, polled at its refresh period while a widget that called `watchPublicData()` is on screen, otherwise with the message | | In the widget | `chatData`, event `chatDataChanged` | `publicData`, event `publicDataChanged` | The format is the same everywhere (sending, inline results, changes): * The chat state and the shared state are each a text of up to **1024 bytes** (bytes of UTF-8, not characters: 512 Cyrillic letters fill it), often JSON. The server does not interpret it. * At sending, a field not passed means no state. In a change, a field not passed stays as it is, and an empty text clears it. The widget never sees an empty text: a cleared or absent state is `null`. When the bot changes the state, a running widget gets `chatDataChanged` or `publicDataChanged` with the new state already in place (for a shared widget's shared state, only if the widget called `watchPublicData()`). Nothing restarts and the page keeps what it has drawn, so redraw from the state. A change that touches both fires both, `chatDataChanged` first. A change that leaves one of them as it was fires nothing for it. ``` const W = window.TelegramWidget; function render() { let game = null; try { game = JSON.parse(W.chatData); } catch (e) {} // … draw from the chat state (null: no state yet) } W.onEvent('chatDataChanged', render); render(); ``` #### Static and shared widgets | Property | Static widget | Shared widget | | --- | --- | --- | | Created by | `sendWidget` without `is_shared` | the first `sendWidget` (or inline send) with `is_shared` | | Code, size, request flag | in the message | in the shared widget, the same in every message that shows it | | Shared state (`public_data`) | in the message. A forward gets a copy as of the moment of forwarding, and a change reaches only the original | in the shared widget: one shared state for every message and forward, changed for all of them at once | | Chat state (`chat_data`) | per message | per message, set at each send | | Shown again elsewhere | by forwarding (a frozen copy) | by forwarding, or with [sendSharedWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendsharedwidget) / an [inline result](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#inline-mode-widgets) by its identifier | | Requests from forwards | never | on a tap, if it was sent with `allow_queries`. They arrive as [shared\_widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sharedwidgetquery) | | Identifier | none | `widget.id` in every message that shows it, for everyone including the bot, and `widget_id` in the methods and updates | A shared widget is like a poll: one object that any number of messages refer to. There is no separate method to create one: **the first send creates it.** To get its identifier in advance, to send the widget to many chats or to offer it in inline mode, send it once with `is_shared` to any chat (for example your own chat with the bot) and read `widget.id` from the returned message. * **One widget, one behavior.** Every message showing a shared widget has the same HTML, size and request flag, as one poll cannot be anonymous in one message and public in another. Only the chat state belongs to each message. * **Permanent.** A shared widget outlives every message that shows it: its shared state stays, [editSharedWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editsharedwidgetdata) edits it by its identifier after every carrier is deleted, and requests from live forwards keep arriving. * **Immutable code.** For a new layout, send a new widget with `sendWidget`, which makes a new shared widget. Messages that show the old one keep it. | Send | Use case | Shared state | Forwards may ask the bot | Change the shared state | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `sendWidget` | a widget with state | in the message, forwards get a copy | No | by the original's coordinates, only the original changes | | `sendWidget` + `is_shared` | a ticker | a new shared widget | No, forwards follow it | by `widget_id` or by any original's coordinates | | `sendWidget` + `is_shared` + `allow_queries` | live forwards (a poll) | a new shared widget | Yes, on a tap | by `widget_id` or by any original's coordinates | | `sendSharedWidget` | send an existing shared widget again | the shared widget's, unchanged by the send | per the shared widget's flag | by `widget_id` or by any original's coordinates | **Freshness.** An edit of a shared widget is visible at once to every read: opening the chat or scrolling to the message gives the current shared state. A widget already on screen gets a new shared state only if it asks for it with `TelegramWidget.watchPublicData()`. While at least one widget that called it is on screen, the app polls that shared widget (one poll per shared widget, whatever the number of messages showing it) at the shared widget's refresh period, and every widget on screen showing it gets `publicDataChanged`. A widget that does not watch gets its shared state only with the message. `unwatchPublicData()` stops asking. Both are synchronous, need no tap, can be called at any time and may be repeated. On a static widget they do nothing (its shared state, like every chat state, is pushed anyway), and a preview never watches. The refresh period is a property of the shared widget: 30 seconds when created, changed only with `cache_time` in [editSharedWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editsharedwidgetdata) (5-3600 seconds: less than 5 is refused, more than 3600 is clamped). Choose it for how often the shared state changes: about 10 seconds for a price, minutes or an hour for something that changes slowly. **Keep the newest state.** A poll can bring a shared state older than one the widget already drew from a request's answer or an earlier poll, and counts would jump back and forth. Put a revision in the shared state (`"r": 41`, raised on every edit, and in the answer too) and have the widget ignore anything older than the newest it has seen. #### Widgets in groups Bots can send widgets to basic groups and supergroups they are members of, forum topics included ([test server only](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability)). The bot needs the right to send other messages (`can_send_other_messages` in [ChatPermissions](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#chatpermissions): animations, games, stickers and inline bots). Widgets are checked like messages sent via an inline bot, so a group that does not give the bot this right refuses the widget too. Channels refuse widgets, sent directly or via the bot. In a group: * **The chat state is shared by all members.** Everyone sees the same chat state. Draw it per user with `TelegramWidget.viewer.id` (chess for two is one widget and one chat state). * **Requests run on a tap only**, never in the background. * **The bot addresses the message as usual**: the `chat` and `message_id` of a [widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) are the ones it uses for its other messages in that group, and [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata) takes the same pair. #### Inline mode widgets A bot with inline mode enabled can return widgets as inline results ([test server only](h", "offset": 20816, "next_offset": 32316, "total_characters": 108039 }

item.text: В актуальном Bot API есть метод `sendWidget`, доступный для личных чатов. Для этого счётчика достаточно одного запроса: кнопка будет менять число внутри виджета, сохраняя его на устройстве пользователя для этого сообщения.
